pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 LISTENING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How should we listen for specific information from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to information from oral texts for communication
2. use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences
3. recognise listening for information as a crucial aspect of communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 LISTENING FOR INFORMATION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 LISTENING FOR INFORMATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Respond to information from oral texts for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to information from oral texts for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to information from oral texts for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to information from oral texts for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise listening for information as a crucial aspect of communication

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise listening for information as a crucial aspect of communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise listening for information as a crucial aspect of communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise listening for information as a crucial aspect of communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond to information from oral texts for communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information to a partner. (skill: use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: recognise listening for information as a crucial aspect of communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond to information from oral texts for communication.
3. Practise this skill: use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences.
4. Practise this skill: recognise listening for information as a crucial aspect of communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How should we listen for specific information from a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond to information from oral texts for communication.
5. Be able to: use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
